prompts: A policy newsletter is running a piece on which of Brazil's anti-inflation plans delivered what it promised, and wants a ranking it can defend. Research the plans in {WS}/RUBRIC.md on the open web: this one needs public sources, and you are allowed to browse. Score every plan with that rubric, rank the top 3, and write a one-page dossier for the editor in {WS}/dossier.md. Every number must carry the URL it came from. Record the result in {WS}/result.json: plans (one entry per plan with plan, launch_date, ipca_before, ipca_after, months_lasted, score and sources, a list of URLs) and top3 (plan names, best first).
answers:
[goal] Rank Brazil’s anti-inflation plans using the supplied rubric.

[action] Scored every plan and saved the [editor’s dossier](./dossier.md) and [structured results](./result.json). Launch dates follow the public rollout. For Real, that means the day the currency entered circulation.

[result] **Real ranked first, followed by Collor I and Collor II.** The calculation check returned `Real 0,9937 > Collor I 0,5823 > Collor II 0,4217`. I verified the annual inflation figures against [IBGE’s historical IPCA table](https://www.ibge.gov.br/biblioteca/visualizacao/periodicos/236/inpc_ipca_2012_jan.pdf) and recalculated the scores from the cited launch dates and the [rubric](./RUBRIC.md).

[next] The editorial caveat is that Collor I’s post-launch inflation window includes Collor II. The ranking measures observed inflation and time between listed launches. It cannot isolate either plan’s effect. [Collor II announcement](https://atlas.fgv.br/verbete/6296)

# Brazil’s anti-inflation plans

**Editor’s finding.** Real ranks first, followed by Collor I and Collor II. Real combined the largest proportional fall in annual inflation with the rubric’s maximum durability credit. Collor I placed second on a larger measured inflation drop than Collor II. Its post-launch calendar year also includes Collor II, so the fall cannot be attributed to Collor I alone. Collor II’s score benefits from the long gap to Real, even though its post-launch annual inflation stayed above four digits. **How to read the scores.** The IPCA columns use IBGE’s national calendar-year rates for the year before and the year after launch. The score weights the proportional decline at 70% and durability at 30%. Rising inflation earns zero decline credit. Durability is elapsed whole months to the next launch listed in the rubric, capped at 60 months, with 60 assigned to Real. A month counts once the launch-day anniversary is reached, using month-end if that day does not exist. Scores are displayed to four decimals and ordered by the underlying calculation. }
$rank = $r.plans | Sort-Object score -Descending | Select-Object -First 3
if (($rank.plan -join '"' > ') -ne ("'$r.top3 -join '"' > ')) { throw 'Ranking mismatch' }
